name: Memcached
tagline: The original multi-threaded, dead-simple distributed memory cache for key-value blobs.
description: Memcached is a multi-threaded, in-memory cache that does one thing: store opaque values under keys with an expiry, evicting by LRU when memory runs out. There is no persistence, replication or server-side clustering; clients hash keys across a pool of independent nodes. That simplicity is its strength, and it still runs some of the largest cache fleets in the world. Modern releases add an extstore flash tier, TLS, a meta-command protocol and a built-in proxy for routing and replication. Pick it when you need a pure cache with predictable latency and nothing else.

pricing.notes: Free; managed by ElastiCache and Google Memorystore for Memcached.

scale.notes: Scales by adding nodes and client-side consistent hashing; the built-in proxy can route and replicate. Meta and Netflix run fleets of thousands of nodes.

strengths: Multi-threaded design uses every core on a box with very little tuning
Extremely predictable latency and memory behaviour with slab allocation
Extstore spills cold items to NVMe to cut RAM cost
Protocol supported by nearly every web framework and language
Tiny operational surface: no persistence, no replication state to manage
weaknesses: No persistence: a restart empties the cache
Only opaque blobs; no data structures, queries or server-side scripting
No built-in replication or failover outside the proxy
Item size limit (1 MB default) and no secondary access paths
useCases: Read-through caching of database query results
Session storage when losing sessions is acceptable
Very large, horizontally sharded look-aside cache tiers
notIdealFor: Any data you cannot afford to lose
Queues, pub/sub or counters with complex semantics
Rich data structures (use Redis or Valkey)
